claim: FLARE's line-level suspiciousness diagnostic model, used to guide iterative code refinement, beats NL-Debugging by 1.72-7.42 percentage points absolute Pass@1 in 9 of 10 (base LLM x benchmark) settings on LiveCodeBench and BigCodeBench; searching the top-10 suspicious lines (k=10) adds another +8.50pp average over k=1.
stance_target: downstream utility of fine-grained/localized code-error signals for improving generation quality via targeted repair
scope_conditions: LiveCodeBench and BigCodeBench, 5 base LLMs, iterative code refinement setting
quoted_support: FLARE(k=1) beats NL-Debugging by 1.72-7.42 pp absolute Pass@1 in 9/10 settings; FLARE(k=10) adds another +8.50pp average.

claim: FLARE's diagnostic model is a separate lightweight bidirectional transformer trained from scratch on Collu-Bench, not the code-generating LLM's own self-reported confidence -- the coder LLM plays no role in producing the suspiciousness signal.
stance_target: differentiation of FLARE's mechanism from DPRC's native self-expressed confidence
quoted_support: This is a SEPARATE diagnostic model, not the code-generating LLM's own self-reported confidence -- the coder LLM plays no role in producing the suspiciousness signal itself.

claim: FLARE's localization granularity is spatial (which lines/AST lexical units are buggy), not per-test-case (which hidden unit test will fail) -- its standalone diagnostic model reaches 67% Top-1 / 89% Top-10 line-localization accuracy, beating FlexFL, LLMAO, and BAP fault-localization baselines, but the paper reports no AUROC for confidence discrimination.
stance_target: DPRC's differentiation on localization axis (per-requirement/per-test vs per-line)
scope_conditions: line-level fault localization on Collu-Bench-derived buggy solutions
quoted_support: the localization axis is SPATIAL/TEXTUAL (which code lines/spans will be edited), not PER-TEST-CASE... The diagnostic model alone reaches 67% Top-1 / 89% Top-10 localization accuracy, beating FlexFL, LLMAO, and BAP fault-localization baselines
